findings.summary: Several modules bypass config/index.ts barrel for types that are re-exported from it
evidence: cli/sync-command.ts:84 imports 'Config' from '../config/types.js' but Config is exported from config/index.ts:31
lifecycle/types.ts:2 imports 'RepoConfig' from '../config/types.js' but RepoConfig is exported from config/index.ts:30
lifecycle/repo-lifecycle-manager.ts:8 imports 'RepoConfig' from '../config/types.js' instead of config/index.js
lifecycle/lifecycle-helpers.ts:4 imports 'RepoConfig, GitHubRepoSettings' from '../config/types.js' -- both available in barrel
sync/sync-workflow.ts:1 and sync/file-sync-strategy.ts:1 import RepoConfig from '../config/types.js' instead of barrel
findings.suggestion: Update these imports to use '../config/index.js' instead of '../config/types.js'. This consolidates cross-module access through the barrel and makes boundary adherence consistent. For sync/types.ts and sync/file-writer.ts, the FileContent/ContentValue imports are legitimately necessary (not in barrel), so those stay.

findings.summary: FileContent and ContentValue types consumed cross-module but not exported from config/index.ts barrel
evidence: Neither FileContent nor ContentValue appear in config/index.ts re-exports
findings.suggestion: Add 'FileContent' and 'ContentValue' to the type re-exports in src/config/index.ts, then update sync/file-writer.ts and sync/types.ts to import from '../config/index.js'. This brings these cross-module types under the barrel's governance.

findings.summary: 11 test files use non-strict assert import instead of the dominant strict pattern
evidence: 84 test files use 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"' while these 11 files use 'import assert from "node:assert"'
The non-strict imports are concentrated in vcs/ test files (7 of 11) plus 4 scattered utility tests, suggesting they were written in a batch without following the established convention
findings.suggestion: Change all 11 files to use 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"' to match the dominant convention. This is a mechanical find-and-replace change.
